title: Build a pocket rival
kicker: A practical first build for a hobbyist alone, a hobbyist with a mentor, or a design team taking it to product
items: THE OBJECT
A black, crimson and ochre practice companion with a round pixel pet, activity XP, a tuner and five single-note drills.
THE FIRST BUILD
Teensy 4.1 + Audio Adapter + Adafruit 6178. USB power, one buffered audio input, two finger buttons and one momentary footswitch.
THE STATUS
Real CAD and original firmware source are included. Geometry and desktop logic checks are separate from the physical tests done on a bench.
WHO CHECKS

Where this guide says mentor, read: an experienced second person, such as a mentor, a maker-space volunteer or a studio engineer. Building alone is covered in docs/SOLO_BUILD.md; the product brief for a studio is docs/STUDIO_BRIEF.md.
check: Start with pages 2-3. Buy the bench electronics first; print the final enclosure after measurement and screen tests.

title: The first bench session
kicker: Suggested 2-hour session, alone or with a mentor; bring this pack and the actual parts
items: 00-20 MIN / REVIEW
Confirm the USB-only sensing architecture, display choice and source of buffered dry guitar. Review the input attenuator before connecting the rig.
20-50 MIN / LEARN
Practise one solder joint. Identify switch lugs and trimmer wiper with a meter. Mark every power and signal wire before soldering.
50-100 MIN / MAKE
Upload Stage 1. Add the display and buttons, then upload Stage 2. Get VEX and the control readings working on the desk.
100-120 MIN / DECIDE
Measure screen readability, the purchased boards and connector bodies. Record changes in the measurement sheet and assign the next session.
check: First-session success = a working screen and controls, plus a measured list of remaining fit questions.

title: Build in three milestones
kicker: Each milestone produces something usable and teaches one new layer
items: 1 / PET ON THE DESK
USB + screen + buttons. Learn power, ground, SPI, upload and button debouncing. No guitar connection is needed yet.
2 / LISTEN TO GUITAR
Add the audio board and attenuator. Learn signal level, RMS, clipping and calibration. Keep the existing audible guitar path.
3 / ENCLOSE + USE
Fit the real parts, assemble the case, route wires and verify readability and strength. Then test the companion alongside your rig.
check: R1 does not provide audio bypass, silent muting, 9V pedal power, MIDI control, daily streaks or chord/polyphonic scoring.

title: The important design choices
kicker: Read this before ordering or printing
items: REAL SCREEN SIZE
Adafruit 6178 has a 1.28-inch round screen: approximately 32.4mm visible diameter. It is smaller than the concept art, chosen for a documented SPI driver.
REAL CASE SIZE
The body is 86 x146 x45mm; controls extend higher. This is not a drop-in replacement for a compact pedal tuner. Use a paper footprint on your pedalboard first.
PLAIN OPTICS + POWER
R1 uses a flat clear disc and direct USB power. A dome and protected pedalboard 9V conversion are later engineering changes.
FOOT LOAD
An aluminum plate sits on four columns below the switch. The printed prototype starts with hand operation; a load test with the electronics removed comes before foot use.
check: If the 32mm display fails the standing test, choose a larger screen before committing to this enclosure.

title: Where guitar audio goes
kicker: The companion listens on a separate branch
items: 1 / FIND A DRY FEED

Use a buffered tuner or auxiliary output on your multi-effects or pedal, and test that it stays live in every preset you play. If it mutes or switches off during playing, use a dedicated buffered splitter output.
2 / KEEP THE MAIN ROUTE
Guitar -> buffer or splitter -> your existing amp or modeller route. The companion has no audio output and does not replace that route.
3 / CONNECT THE LISTENER
Buffered dry output -> J1 -> attenuator -> Audio Adapter LINE IN L. No raw passive-pickup input, amplifier speaker output or phantom-powered input.
WHY
A clean branch avoids scoring reverb repeats or synthesized notes. It also keeps experimental firmware out of your audible guitar path.
check: With the companion disconnected, the original rig should work exactly as before. Log what the rig's tuner mute does to the dry feed.

title: Wire the display
kicker: Use the board silkscreen names, not cable colors or a guessed pin order
check: Teensy logic is 3.3V. Display VIN is an input; display 3Vo is an output and is left disconnected.
rows: Do not connect display 3Vo output to Teensy 3.3V.
Hardware SPI clock; onboard LED activity is normal.
Display select; audio SD uses pin10.
Keep unused display SD card deselected; no SD card in R1.

title: Wire the controls
kicker: Test every switch before connecting it to a GPIO
items: 1 / IDENTIFY CONTACTS
Remove power. In continuity mode, the selected pair must be open when released and close only while pressed. Use SPST normally-open momentary switches.
2 / CONNECT
MODE -> pin0; QUEST -> pin1; FOOT -> pin2. The other lug of each switch goes to GND. Insulate all solder lugs.
3 / ADD THE LED
Pin9 -> 1k resistor R3 -> LED anode. Cathode -> GND. Identify polarity before trimming the leads.
WHY
INPUT_PULLUP holds the released pin HIGH. A press connects it to ground, so firmware reads LOW.
check: Unpowered: the switch wire is not shorted to any power rail. Stage 2 must show exactly one changing input per press.

title: Build the audio attenuator
kicker: Have a second person check this small circuit before connection to the rig
items: 1 / IDENTIFY THE TRIMMER
Bourns 3386P-1-103LF is 10k. Meter terminals1-3: approximately10k. Terminal2 is the wiper; its resistance to either end changes as you turn.
2 / WIRE THE DIVIDER
TIP -> R1 10k -> terminal3. Terminal1 -> ground. Wiper2 -> R2 1k -> LINE IN L. Jack sleeve -> LINE IN ground.
3 / BEGIN AT MINIMUM
Set the wiper near terminal1 using the meter. Check continuity and shorts, then begin Stage3 with a quiet known line-level source.
WHY
The divider lowers the signal before conversion. Its maximum unloaded output is half the input; codec loading reduces it further. It is not a general overvoltage protector.
check: The audio board has its own input coupling. Use LINE IN L/GND labels; neither MIC nor headphone ground is a substitute.

title: Assemble and check the audio stack
kicker: Short aligned headers carry the fast audio clocks
items: 1 / ORIENT
Use the PJRC Rev D/D2 pin diagram. Align the shared 14-pin rows with the matching printed Teensy pin numbers; do not align by the board edges alone.
2 / SOLDER + INSPECT
Socket the stack for service. Keep the audio clocks on short headers. Check every row for bridges with magnification and continuity.
3 / CHECK POWER
USB unplugged: inspect the 3.3V/GND pair for a sustained short. USB on: black probe to GND, red to 3.3V; target3.20-3.40V. Stop if a board heats abnormally.
RESERVED PINS
Audio7/8/20/21/23; I2C18/19. Pins6 and10 are held HIGH to deselect optional audio-board memory and SD. No SD cards in R1.
check: Verify display + audio-board current against the Teensy regulator budget. Record the measured header gap; CAD currently reserves9.4mm.

title: Upload 1: prove USB on your Mac
kicker: One sketch, four stages: change VEX_STAGE in config.h
items: 1 / INSTALL
Install Arduino IDE2 from arduino.cc. In Arduino IDE > Settings, add the PJRC boards URL listed in docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md; install Teensy using Boards Manager.
2 / LIBRARIES
Install Adafruit GC9A01A, Adafruit GFX and Adafruit BusIO using Library Manager. Audio, Wire, SPI and EEPROM come with Teensy support.
3 / OPEN + SELECT
Open firmware/VEX_Pocket_Rival/VEX_Pocket_Rival.ino. Choose Teensy4.1, USB Type Serial, normal600MHz. Leave VEX_STAGE1 for the first upload.
4 / VERIFY + UPLOAD

Click Verify, then Upload. Select the Teensy port. If prompted, press the physical Program button. Open Serial Monitor at115200. From a terminal the same steps are make firmware STAGE=1, make upload STAGE=1, make monitor.
check: Onboard LED blinks and Serial says VEX USB OK. No .hex is supplied: the complete target build still needs this verification.

title: Upload 2: screen and buttons
kicker: Disconnect USB before adding each wiring group
items: 1 / CONNECT
Add display wires W01-W10 and controls W11-W14. Keep SPI wires short, initially under100mm. Leave audio input disconnected.
2 / UPLOAD

Set VEX_STAGE2, Verify and Upload. The display should show the bat and live M/Q/F button states. Serial prints one JSON line a second: flush_us is the time to draw and send one cadence, tx_bytes the rows sent. Type f, b, 1 or 2 in the monitor to compare full-frame, band-diff and 100 vs 200ms redraws.
3 / EXERCISE
Press each control ten times. One state changes from0 to1 while held, and returns to0 on release. FOOT also lights the status LED.
IF IT FAILS
White screen: check VIN/GND, CS/DC/reset and SPI pins. Stuck input: inspect the chosen lug pair. Rotated display: change setRotation, not wiring.
check: Put the display at the real pedalboard distance. Confirm legibility before fabricating the enclosure.

title: Upload 3: audio and level
kicker: Begin with a known low-level line source; then test the buffered guitar feed
items: 1 / START SMALL
Set VEX_STAGE3. Codec input level stays0, the least sensitive setting (3.12Vpp full scale). Trimmer begins at minimum.
2 / OBSERVE
Serial must report codec=1. Slowly raise the trimmer while playing. Aim for peaks roughly0.10-0.80 during strong playing; 0.98 means clipping.
3 / COMPARE GUITARS

Test each guitar you will practise with separately, for example one with active and one with passive pickups. Record trim position, peak and quiet RMS. Choose a setting that avoids clipping any of them.
IF IT FAILS
codec=0: inspect3.3V, GND and I2C18/19. Flat-zero audio: inspect LINE IN L, input ground and short I2S headers. Low signal: confirm source before increasing gain.
check: Confirm audible rig noise does not change with USB connected. Avoid correcting hum by disconnecting protective mains earth.

title: Upload 4: bring VEX to life
kicker: Participation XP and one reward per completed practice session
items: 1 / CALIBRATE
Set VEX_STAGE4 and upload. Mute the strings, then hold QUEST for1.2s. Remain quiet for3s. Calibration pauses counting and runs again after every boot.
2 / PRACTISE
Tap FOOT to start. Detected playing earns10XP per active minute. Silence, pause, clipping and stale audio do not earn time. A completed goal earns one fragment.
3 / SAVE
Tap FOOT to pause. Hold MODE until Saved appears before unplugging. The two-record save scheme checks CRC and retains the previous valid record if one write tears.
LIMIT
Automatic saves wait for quiet gaps after60s. Abrupt power loss can lose the unsaved portion of a continuous session. This is activity detection, not proof of musical quality.
check: Complete a5-minute active goal, verify one fragment, save and reboot. Confirm totals persist and startup is paused.

title: Understand the CAD
kicker: A real assembly, with explicit limits on purchased-part models
items: OPEN
Import VEX_Pocket_Rival_Assembly.step into Fusion. It contains separate named components. STEP preserves geometry, not the Python feature history.
EDIT
build_cad.py is the parametric source. Base/lid width and length are linked; component positions and cutouts also appear as explicit construction values. Re-run checks after edits.
DATUM
Origin is the footprint centre on the underside. +Y points toward rear sockets; +Z points up. The faceplate spans z42-45mm.
EVIDENCE
Display model is manufacturer CAD. Teensy/audio models are community references. Button, footswitch, jack, headers and trimmer include labeled simplified envelopes.
check: Use named part files for fabrication. Do not print the combined assembly, commercial electronics, wire reserves or the clear-window STL.

title: Measure and print a coupon first
kicker: A cheap fit check before a full case print
items: 1 / MEASURE
Record body envelopes, threaded shafts, nut thickness, plug size and solder tails. The jack body is a reserve, not a verified model. Confirm its nut grips the3mm rear wall.
2 / PRINT

Print Fit_Coupon.stl flat at100% scale. Try the M3 clearance,7.2mm button hole,12.4mm switch hole,9.8mm jack hole and M3 nut pocket. Enter the results in measurements.csv; make measure-check lists which parts are ready to print.
3 / ADJUST
Use calipers and the coupon to set printer clearances. A nut should seat by hand; a threaded control should pass without force. Change the CAD if purchased parts differ.
4 / PRINT THE CASE
Suggested starting point: PETG,0.2mm layers,5perimeters,6top/bottom layers,35% infill. This is a print trial, not a structural rating.
check: Only measured-fit approval releases the full print. Print base open-side up; faceplate/tray flat; bezel pocket facing up.

title: Assembly 1: base and rear input
kicker: A_base + case/tray nuts + Q_input_jack
items: PARTS
Base A;8M3 captive nuts; Switchcraft111X and included hardware; USB cable. File the test print gently; remove debris.
1 / INSERT NUTS
Seat4case nuts at the top corner posts and4tray nuts near the floor. Confirm each screw starts freely before installing electronics.
2 / FIT INPUT
Insert the jack from inside through the rear9.8mm hole. Add the stock washer/nut outside. Rotate lugs away from the board area and tighten without twisting wires.
3 / TEST USB ACCESS
Feed the selected USB plug through the service opening and check that it can reach the Teensy connector. The opening is not a panel-mounted USB socket.
check: Jack cannot rotate; stock threads have proper engagement; cable and corner posts clear the measured jack body.

title: Assembly 2: removable electronics
kicker: E_tray + F_Teensy + G_audio + R_input board
items: PARTS
Tray E;3x15mm audio spacers;2x6mm perfboard spacers; associated M2 hardware;4M3x6 tray screws;2small nylon ties.
1 / BUILD ON THE DESK
Attach the socketed Teensy/audio stack. Secure the Teensy through the tray slots with ties clear of components. Install the audio spacers at the three modeled holes.
2 / INPUT BOARD
Cut/drill the14x28mm perfboard; fit the trimmer and resistors, then inspect wiring. Mount it on the6mm spacers. Keep solder tails off the tray and adjacent PCB.
3 / INSTALL
Lower the tested carrier into the base and fasten the four tray screws. Preserve access to USB and Program; avoid clamping any wire under the tray.
check: Rerun Stage3 before adding the lid. No carrier flex; no metal fastener touches a trace or solder joint.

title: Assembly 3: display and finger controls
kicker: Build the lid assembly while its underside is accessible
items: PARTS
Faceplate B; display H; two 2.0mm spacers; two M2x10 countersunk screws and nuts; two COM-11992 buttons; LED.
1 / DISPLAY
Place the display behind the opening with its solder-header tail toward the buttons. Put the2mm spacers between the front PCB mounting pads and the faceplate underside.
2 / RETAIN
Seat the M2 countersunk heads flush in the faceplate, then fit nuts below the PCB. Verify flushness before adding the window. Tighten gently; do not load the glass or flex tail.
3 / CONTROLS
Fit MODE and QUEST with stock nuts. Insulate leads and leave service length. Fit the LED without adhesive covering its leads or adjacent contacts.
check: Measured display holes should be22.86mm apart. Confirm screen centring and no contact between lid and display glass.

title: Footswitch retention detail
kicker: Local cutaway of the faceplate; parts separated vertically for clarity
items: FROM BELOW
Momentary switch N -> lower retaining nut -> aluminum plate M. The nut meets the underside of the plate.
THROUGH THE LID
The threaded bushing passes through the plate and faceplate B. Fit the stock washer and upper nut above the lid.
SUPPORT
When the lid closes, the plate rests on the four base columns. Verify contact at all four locations; the display is not part of this load path.
OPTIONAL CAP
The crimson cap lifts off for service. Leave it out unless its fit and full switch travel are confirmed. Validate the structure before foot use.
check: This illustration explains assembly order. It is not a force rating; use the exact purchased switch and hardware for the fit test.

title: Assembly 4: footswitch and window
kicker: Separate the screen cover from the foot-load path
items: 1 / FOOTSWITCH
On the switch bushing: lower nut ->2mm aluminum plate ->3mm lid ->top washer ->top nut. Position the plate so it rests on all four base columns when closed.
2 / WINDOW
Place the40x1mm clear disc in the bezel pocket. It has0.3mm nominal radial and axial allowance. Use only a thin peripheral anti-rattle gasket, never pressure on the LCD.
3 / BEZEL
Fasten charcoal C with4M3x12 screws and nuts. Bond W gold rim into its shallow recess and W crimson cheek beside C with thin adhesive. Keep the cap clear of full travel.
WHY
The replaceable window protects the display. The plate spreads switch force into the base. Both need physical fit and load tests.
check: No screen pressure when screws tighten. Hand-actuate the switch through its full travel before any foot test.

title: Assembly 5: harness, close and test
kicker: Finish with service access and repeatable checks
items: 1 / ROUTE
Keep the shielded analog pair short and away from display/SPI wires. Use the right-side wire lane. Add heat shrink at every exposed solder lug and resistor lead.
2 / SERVICE LOOP
Leave enough slack to lift the lid about50mm and rest it beside the base without pulling display wires. Add strain relief without loading a connector.
3 / CLOSE
Inspect from every side while lowering the lid. If it resists, reopen and find the obstruction. Tighten4M3x10 case screws evenly; do not force the printed posts.
4 / ACCEPT
Run the CSV acceptance log: electrical, software, optical, mechanical, thermal and rig-noise checks. Keep your existing tuner until the new tuner passes reference tests.
check: A valid STEP does not establish real wiring clearance or foot strength. Whoever runs each physical test signs the checked_by column.

title: Develop it after the first working build
kicker: Small code changes with observable results
items: 1 / PERSONALITY
Edit the PNG/JSON art in art/ and run tools/make_sprites.py to regenerate the headers, then make sim-build and tools/render_screen.py. Shared ui.h renders the pet on desktop and device.
2 / A NEW REWARD
Change quest rules in core.h. Add a test proving the reward happens once at the threshold and persists after save/restore. Run tests before uploading.
3 / BETTER CHALLENGES
Five single-note drills live in drill_*.h (docs/DRILLS.md) with Skills bests separate from XP. Test noise, chords and wrong notes before trusting a new drill.
4 / HARDWARE NEXT
Larger screen, dome, MIDI or9V power each needs a new wiring/CAD revision. Freeze the working R1 files and change one subsystem at a time.
check: No new feature should silently change pin ownership, saved-record layout or the meaning of a practice score.

title: What has been checked
kicker: Understand what the package proves and what the bench will prove
items: COMPUTER CHECKS
Valid CAD solids and STEP re-import; all-component overlap checks including fasteners; source-derived display mounts; host tests of counting, rewards, pitch math, saves and button logic.
NOT YET PROVEN
Actual display/audio behavior, component revisions, wiring clearance, electrical noise, temperature, lens readability and enclosure strength.
TARGET BUILD EVIDENCE

make setup-firmware and make firmware-all compile all four stages without hardware (passes locally, 20 Nov 2026). Display timing is instrumented (flush_us, tx_bytes) but unmeasured until a board is on the bench.
PHYSICAL RELEASE
Review all purchased parts and the input circuit; complete the log before guitar/foot use. A successful desktop test is useful evidence, not a hardware certificate.
check: See hardware/generated/checks/ and GitHub Actions. Compile success and physical acceptance are separate evidence.

title: Review and edit the grouped CAD
kicker: Five service groups keep related hardware together
items: OPEN THE ASSEMBLY
Use hardware/generated/VEX_Pocket_Rival_Assembly.step: Chassis, Front Panel, Electronics Carrier, Rear IO and Footswitch. Separate subassembly exports and a flat fallback are also supplied.
EDIT THE SOURCE
hardware/cad/build_cad.py is the construction source. assembly_tree.py controls ownership. STEP has named solids, not a native Fusion feature timeline.
CHECK THE RESULT
Run make cad cad-check. R1.1 passes72component validity,2556pairwise overlap checks and grouped STEP re-import. Real parts still require measurement.
PERSONALITY
The charcoal clipped bezel, thin gold ring, crimson cheek and original pixel bat are small practical additions. Keep the actual32.4mm display size.
check: See docs/CAD_REVIEW.md for coordinates, file roles and modification constraints.

title: Try the device before hardware arrives
kicker: Shared C++ practice logic and screen renderer run locally
items: RUN
From the repo: make test, then make sim. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765. Emscripten builds the shared firmware to WebAssembly; no Arduino toolchain is needed for the simulator.
EXERCISE
Follow the Step-by-step guide through First Run and the five guitar drills, or test silence, clipping, tuner, Save, Reboot and torn-write recovery.
COMPILE
Install Arduino CLI; make setup-firmware; make firmware-all. This compiles all four stages with pinned dependencies and never uploads.
UNDERSTAND THE LIMIT
The browser runs the shared C++ App, YIN/onset analyzer, NoteTracker, drills and renderer; it does not emulate the codec, USB noise, switches or screen optics.
WITH A TEENSY ATTACHED
make sim DEVICE=auto opens the Device tab: the real panel mirrored over USB beside the simulator frame, a pixel diff, the serial switches and telemetry sparklines.
check: See docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md for Mac setup, dependencies, staged Verify/Upload instructions and the bench loop.
